𝑫𝒆𝒂𝒅 𝑰𝒔𝒍𝒂𝒏𝒅 is a mostly mediocre game made fun by co-op.

I played this game back in the PS3 days and decided to give it another go for nostalgic reasons, and while I still had fun and enjoyed it a lot, it has some glaring issues.

Firstly, the good stuff:

I enjoy the gameplay a lot. I love jump kicking zombies, I love crafting mods and I enjoy looting unique or exceptional items. I think the concept of having a zombie outbreak in a tropical island is fantastic and it definitely stands out. I am also a big fan of co-op, and this game encourages it immensely — 𝑫𝒆𝒂𝒅 𝑰𝒔𝒍𝒂𝒏𝒅 is a lot more fun when played with friends. This remaster looks beautiful and definitely does the game justice.

The combat can be frustrating at times but it also feels rewarding — using a machete to cut the zombies' heads off, cutting off a thug's limbs, or setting a horde of zombies on fire with a Molotov does something to me. My co-op partner called me a sadist!
The DLC arenas are also very fun and enjoyable and I am glad they are included in this version.

Finally, even 11 years later, that intro is still sick.

Now, for the bad stuff:

If you are looking for a good story, look elsewhere. This game's plot is atrocious and so is most of the voice acting. Even the cutscenes are badly put together and the facial animations leave a lot to desire.

The soundtrack is a bit of a let down as well. Besides the trailer theme, Sam B's 𝑾𝒉𝒐 𝑫𝒐 𝒀𝒐𝒖 𝑽𝒐𝒐𝒅𝒐𝒐 and a very small percentage of the in-game tracks, most of it is very generic.

In terms of world-building there is not much either. The collectibles do not enhance the lore at all nor are they fun or interesting to read. All side quests follow a recurring pattern of fetching items, saving people, and escorting survivors.
There are also quite a few side quests called "continuous events" which award you XP for delivering certain items to the quest giver over and over — I did not see the point of this at all and found 99% of them to be useless.
I completed all the side quests, but by the end of it I could not stomach it any longer, and I started skipping most of the dialogue, which was always the same.

𝑫𝒆𝒂𝒅 𝑰𝒔𝒍𝒂𝒏𝒅 is also infested with bugs, not just zombies. All this remaster did was enhance the graphics (textures, lighting) but they did not bother to fix actual gameplay issues, such as:

• Suddenly dying for no reason (sometimes because of being stuck between objects)
• Losing items in your inventory
• Bugged achievements
• Clunky car controls on keyboard (many times the car will not turn and you crash)
• Funky textures in some rocks
• Clipping into solid objects
• NPCs blocking the way
• Waypoint not showing the path on the mini-map (not sure if this one is a bug but I would have to reposition it)
• NPCs you have to escort suddenly going back the way they came from while you wait for them to return
• Zombies grabbing you while they are on the ground
• Aim assist cannot be turned off, which makes aiming with the mouse considerably annoying
• NPCs and zombies floating mid-air, sometimes getting stuck
• Sound bugs

A lot more stuff like this happened during my playthrough but I cannot recall it now.

Another negative point is that the characters do not interact with eachother as in, for example, 𝑩𝒐𝒓𝒅𝒆𝒓𝒍𝒂𝒏𝒅𝒔. There is no gameplay dialogue between them, and they barely speak to eachother during cutscenes. Their voice lines are also not synced when playing online, so you rarely hear them talk, and when you do, you and whoever is playing them do not even hear the same voice line.

In conclusion, I think 𝑫𝒆𝒂𝒅 𝑰𝒔𝒍𝒂𝒏𝒅 is a fun game with a few shortcomings. I have a nostalgic bond with this game and I will always cherish it for the fun times it gave me, and I do like the combat, so I can never not recommend it. However, I do strongly suggest that you play it with friends, as it makes it a lot more fun and less of a chore.

A Constructive Review of Dead Island – Mercilessly Compared to the Gold Standard: Plant Vs Zombies: GOTY Edition

Let’s get this out of the way: Dead Island had a trailer that made people weep. It promised emotion, depth, and a serious take on the zombie apocalypse set on a tropical island. And then the game came out… and gave us kickboxing zombies in bikinis, fetch quests, and more weapon repairs than actual survival horror. It’s a decent open-world action-RPG with some strong co-op moments.

But, alas — it’s still not Plant Vs Zombies: GOTY Edition.

Melee Combat vs Tactical Gardening

In Dead Island, your main method of survival is hitting zombies with broomsticks, oars, and electrified machetes that somehow break after three swings. You get stamina bars, clunky swings, and physics-driven combat that’s entertaining until it isn’t. Meanwhile, Plant Vs Zombies: GOTY Edition hands you snow peas, spikeweeds, and doom-shrooms, and trusts you to think, not button-mash. One is strategy with personality. The other is hitting a zombie with a wrench while groaning about weapon durability.

Open World vs Perfect Pacing

Dead Island gives you a lush island to explore, sure — but half of it is spent running between NPCs with the charisma of a damp towel, asking for engine parts or bottles of water. In contrast, Plant Vs Zombies: GOTY Edition wastes zero seconds of your time. It delivers new mechanics every level, clever enemy types, and constant variety. While Dead Island makes you trek across a jungle to repair a boat, Plant Vs Zombies: GOTY Edition hands you a new seed packet and says: “Good luck, genius.”

Co-op vs Core Loop

Yes, Dead Island is fun with friends. You can stomp zombies together, get swarmed together, and laugh at broken ragdoll physics together. But when you strip it down, it’s still a repetitive slog without strong mission design. Plant Vs Zombies: GOTY Edition, on the other hand, doesn’t need friends to be fun. It’s designed so tightly that every click feels satisfying. It’s a solo experience with more polish and precision than a four-player zombie brawler set in paradise.

Tone and Style: Confused vs Cohesive

Dead Island tries to be gritty and emotional, then throws you into sidequests where you’re retrieving champagne for a party girl in a zombie-infested hotel. It’s tonal whiplash. Meanwhile, Plant Vs Zombies: GOTY Edition knows exactly what it is — playful, quirky, smart, and consistent. There’s no identity crisis. Crazy Dave may wear a pot on his head, but he has more vision than every NPC in Dead Island combined.

Progression and Customization

Leveling up in Dead Island means skill trees, weapon mods, and lots of backtracking. But none of that progression feels as tight or rewarding as unlocking a simple kernel-pult in Plant Vs Zombies: GOTY Edition. Every plant you earn is meaningful, every zombie variant requires a new tactic. Meanwhile, in Dead Island, your best strategy remains “kick them repeatedly until they stop moving.”

Dead Island is a decent zombie-smashing RPG with flashes of creativity and a killer soundtrack. But if you're looking for the real pinnacle of zombie game design — the perfect blend of charm, strategy, creativity, and depth — there's only one name that deserves to be etched in granite:

Plant Vs Zombies: GOTY Edition.

Because why fight to survive on an island when you can simply plant a row of sunflowers... and win the war from your lawn?
Back when games were about having fun and not paying for loot boxes and cosmetics... I wish we would go back but I'm afraid its far too late.

Introduced by the legendary teaser trailer, that might as well be one of the best trailers in the history of video games, Dead Island delivers a rather mediocre zombie apocalypse experience. It succeeds in creating a horror atmosphere, given that the game takes place during daytime and is set in a very attractive environment, but fails horribly in narrative and quests.

Most of the time you'll be running simple errands for survivors such as obtaining food, medicine, weapons and shelter. This can be fun, especially in Act I when you are learning the ropes, but quickly becomes boring and repetitive and that is mainly because of how dull and shallow all the dialogues, characters and quest objectives are. There are mainly fetch quests, including bizarre ones like rescuing a teddy bear for a hysterical, grown-up woman. As you are the only immune person on the island, you'll be on your feet most of the time. Exploring on your own loses significance as the game sends you to places you've already explored multiple times and the game world respawns all the items you've collected and the enemies you've killed, sometimes minutes after you left the area.

Killing zombies is the main area the game excels in. The immense number of mainly melee weapons plus the gruesome variety in how to dispatch zombies makes a pleasurable experience from each encounter. The sound of heads hitting the ground and the spouts of blood from cut off limbs make combat satisfying. The carving of undead is the most memorable thing about this game. What is also memorable is the enjoyable atmosphere of the first Act that quickly fades away during Act II when the sewers are introduced as the worst part of this game. The OST plays a big role, especially in safe areas, but is mediocre at best.

The remaster fixes a lot of annoyances I remember from the initial release and beautifies the already great-looking visuals, but there could have been done so much more as there are still many issues with this game. I believe that the game's qualities are multiplied in online co-op.

6.5/10

This was one of the original 'surviving the undead horde' games, taking more than a few cues from Dead Rising but sticking you in a first person perspective and making the whole thing much more immediate and visceral.

The Definitive Edition comes with a few more bells and whistles than the original, a little extra layer of polish that really helps keep the dust off after all these years.  There are times it is a beautiful game, lovely vistas, nice weapon models and decent draw distances.  There are times it is clearly a nine year old game with janky textures, pop-in galore, brain dead AI and whacked out physics.  It manages to dodge all it's problems with a playful sidestep, and just keeps throwing gleeful wicked fun in your face.

On a side note I must make mention of the voice acting.  For the most part it's great.  The player characters are all decent and most of the main NPCs.  Occasionally however you will bump into a side character that is just absolutely hilarious.  Unintentionally so of course.  It's like the voice actor never heard an English (or Spanish, French, Australian etc.) accent before, and just kinda let what they imagined it to be like flow through them.  If you're pedantic you will definitely find much to irritate, but if you go in with the right attitude, there's just so much to enjoy.

I bought Dying Light shortly after completing this, and I look forward to playing that in the future, but for now I have another hundred hours ready to try some co-op and keep the beaches of Banoi safe from the undead menace.

Dead Island Definitive Edition is the re-release of the original Dead Island that released on 6 September 2011, and this version has all of the downloadable content included.

[h1]Characters[/h1]
—There are four people to choose from and they have their strengths and their own special "fury" ability: Sam B. with his fists, Xian Mei with her blade weapons, Logan Carter with throwing weapons, and Purna with her pistol. Ryder White is a character choice; he's the main character in the Ryder White DLC and uses his pistol for fury.

—There are other characters you interact with, but mostly they are part of the story and are kind of forgettable.

—There's one NPC that helps you store items, so cool, I guess?

—NPC repeatable quests? Annoying as hell. Ex: "OH THANK GOD!"

[h1]Atmosphere/Environment[/h1]
—The environments are a wide variety: wide-open, tropical-vista views of the ocean and sunshine; cramped, desolated, blood-ridden areas inside tunnels; and dark, creepy houses and closets. Oh, also, there's a lighthouse.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
—There are so many zombies and so many ways to dispatch them: beat them, kick them, stomp them, shoot them, chop their heads off, throw weapons at them, blow them up with explosives, throw Molotov cocktails at them, use your special ability, electrocute them—SO MANY WAYS, GO F*CKING CRAZY!

—This game is fun exploring and killing zombies alone, but with more people involved it is a BLAST to play through!

—Crafting is amazing in this game; there are so many combinations and types of weapons to craft that can really knock zombies off of their own feet. There are secret blueprints hidden around the world to find, and those are worth the price of discovery and crafting

—You have a skill tree—fury, combat, survival—with lots of new abilities, and the best ones that I recommend are anything that gets you cash, more stamina, durable weapons, and the execution-style head smash. Two feet is the best!

—Ryder White's DLC has a BIG problem with infected zombies; there are so many that appear and chase you that you are placed into a position where you have to get lucky and throw grenades and run away. Despite having effective medkits, health, and stamina, you cannot upgrade Ryder's stats. Thankfully this DLC is shorter than the main game.

—NPC's are kind of helpless when they get surrounded; be sure to throw weapons at the zombies.

[h1]Enemies/Allies[/h1]
—Your zombie rundown is as follows: walkers move slow; infected move fast; straightjacket ones charge you; thin-skinned bubbly ones explode at close range; floaters that move slow and puke on you from a distance; butchers that are a pain to fight and dispatch; and humans that wield pistols, rifles, and shotguns.

—There are a couple of boss fights, one being towards the end of the campaign before [spoiler] you board the helicopter with Charon [/spoiler]

[h1]Story[/h1]
—Beginning intro of someone getting drunk makes no sense character-wise; you just wake up disoriented—probably from too much drinking or someone slipped you a roofie or something—to find that the entire island has been riddled with human-craving zombies due to a mass virus. Surprisingly, you and y our acquaintances are somehow immune. [spoiler] Your crew must then make your way off of the island because it's about to be destroyed by a nuclear strike. [/spoiler] 

[h1]Boss(es)[/h1]
—There are small mini-bosses known as thugs. Each one may have a weakness in their arm, leg, or torso where a critical hit is possible. Be sure to attack those weak points for an easy kill.

[h1]Graphics[/h1]
—As previously mentioned in the Atmosphere category, the visuals in the sunlight on beaches is very pleasant to look at, even on HDR monitors. Everything else that's shot in the dark seems to be low-textured and were meant to be there.

[h1]Music[/h1]
—The music in this game is not memorable, but kind of smoothing as background noise; the menu music is self-explanatory, the ambiance in safe zones are appropriate, and of course the action sequences. The lighthouse one is somber yet peaceful—my second favorite. The main trailer music by Giles Lamb is the most memorable out of all of them.

This review is based on 100% completion and 38.6 hours of gameplay on steam with many more on Xbox. This review will also apply to the original version of this game for the most part.

[h1][b]Recommendation:[/b][/h1]
Would I recommend this game? Yes, it's not a bad zombie game, and one of the first I ever played, so I do have a nostalgic attachment to it. Don’t go in with massive expectations—while back in its day this was an exceptional game, by today’s standards, it would be considered an "okay" or "good" game, it’s more of a good classic. If you're looking for another solid game to add to your collection, this is a good pick-up. But if you're after something more fleshed out, I’d recommend looking at something like [i]Dying Light.[/i]

The main differences with this [i]Definitive Edition[/i] compared to the original are the improved graphics and the inclusion of the DLC. Other than that, you’re basically getting the same experience as the original, so it will feel a bit dated in some areas since it’s an older game. Still, it's good for what it is and will keep you busy for a good few hours.

One thing I’ll point out, which I’m not 100% sure about, is that this game seems to make my PC run a lot harder compared to other games with higher requirements. So, keep that in mind. The only real issues I had were with dynamic lighting, like in the prologue when you first see the infected and have to run away—my game would drop frames and stutter extremely hard. The only fixes were either loading into another area or restarting the game. I also ran into a few bugs: I’d randomly get killed by being thrown into the air by the map, touching an object, or even just getting out of the car. I also had frequent "survivor killed" pop-ups, forcing me to reload a checkpoint or exit the game. This bug occurred when survivors fell through the map and died, even if you’re not near them or have already saved them. Despite these bugs, the game ran surprisingly well overall.

As for gameplay, it can feel clunky and unintuitive at times, which can be frustrating. Some weapons, like two-handed hammers, don’t feel viable because the actions move your screen too much, making me feel nauseous—lots of weapons do this. Combat can also be annoying with zombies pushing you back while still running at you, which can make you get stuck in the wrong animations. The driving is okay—nothing special—but it’s useful for clearing out zombies before getting out.

The co-op/multiplayer runs well, even when connecting with people across the world, which was a pleasant surprise. The only letdown is progression tracking for the person joining the host, as only character progress like levels and loot are kept—story progression is not. You do get a warning about this before joining someone’s game, though.

The [i]Definitive Edition[/i] does offer some nice enhanced graphics, which I think still look good by today’s standards. The lighting especially makes the game look more modern, though some models and elements do still look a bit scuffed. Overall, it does a good job visually.

Lastly, the game’s arena mode isn’t bad, especially in co-op. It’s pretty standard, but it’s a good source of money once you get far enough for special enemies to spawn more frequently.

While I do recommend the game, it goes on sale regularly due to its age, so I’d suggest waiting for a good deal before picking it up.

[h1][b]Achievements: [/b][/h1]
[b][i]There are a few multiplayer/co-op achievements you’ll need to do, one RNG achievement, and one that requires waiting 28 days. To my knowledge, you’ll also need a controller for one of the achievements. (There actually seems to be a workaround for this if you don’t have one, but I can't 100% confirm myself.)[/i][/b]

The achievements are fairly easy in this game. The main ones to watch out for are the multiplayer/co-op achievements, such as needing to play with 10 different individuals and two others that require a full squad [i](3 other players)[/i]. Since this is an older game, finding people to play with might be tricky, but making a post and waiting for people to reach out over time will be the way to go.

There’s also one achievement for using the analogue control settings in the arena, which, to my knowledge, only works with a controller. The controls feel clunky, but it’s not too bad if you do this with another person at a decent level—you can just use jump kicks to get it done quickly. Once you’ve got it, you can switch back to the normal controls. [i](There seems to be a workaround for this where you can select a controller in the settings and then set it to analogue and then switch back to keyboard and mouse, and it will still be in the analogue settings even without a controller, but I personally can't confirm this 100% works though.)[/i]

The arena is a good way to grind out some of the miscellaneous achievements, like specific kills, if you’re cleaning up before moving on to Act 4 or just want to get them done quickly.

For the achievement that requires exploring all areas, I recommend following a guide. There’s a great guide by Xeinok and Ralf in the Steam guides you can check out [b][url= https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=462275305] here. [/url][/b] [i]( It's on the original Dead Islands community guides, so it may be a bit hard to find through Steam itself, but it will come up easily on Google if you just want to find it later on.)[/i]

Some achievements can be a bit tricky to get to pop, but none were too much of an issue for me. If you meet the requirements for an achievement and it unlocks in-game but not on Steam, sometimes you just need to give it a minute, load into another area, unlock another achievement, or simply exit to the main menu and load back in.

Other than that, all the achievements in this game are fairly easy.

Dead Island is a great first person hack and slash zombie game, It takes you around a beautiful tropical island that is infected by a virus that turns humans, It is completely playable in Online Coop

Welcome to Banoi, A Tropical Island resort with its economy completely based on tourism, Big hotels, Tropical scenes, A lot of bars. But most of the island has been untouched by modern society, There are a lot of tribes in the jungle and around the coast. There is even a prison and an acting military. The Island has been struck by a virus that turns humans into zombie like creatures. 

The game starts in a five star hotel on the island there are 4 survivors who seem to be immune to the virus, They all have a very unique backstory and you can play as any one of them. Originally released in 2011, Dead Island was publisher/developer Techland's first leap into open-world survival horror. Today, the company is well known thanks to Dying Light; their follow-up open-world survival horror zombie game that is still going strong even five years post-launch. With that said, Dead Island showcases all of Techland's shortcomings, and now in retrospect the game feels like the alpha release for what would later be developed. With that said, it has still managed to garner a cult following over the years, and it does offer up some vibrant and unique scenery.

There isn't much of a story to be had here, as this is your typical zombie slaughter-fest of a game. Upon starting a campaign, you're able to pick from four survivors, each with their own skill specialization; ex-football super star Logan Carter (throwing weapons), rapper Sam B (blunt weapons), Chinese government spy Xian Mei (edged weapons), and ex-police officer Purna (firearms) each have backstories of tragedy and loss. They've all come to the tropical island paradise of Banoi to take part in a high-profile party, but somewhere within the night most of the population have fallen ill to a contagious, ravenous plague. As they are overcome by one of the infected, they're rescued by a lifeguard named John Sinamoi, and soon the survivors discover that they're immune to the infectious disease ravaging the resort. After a bit of time, a voice comes on over the radio and promises salvation by flying them off the island if they manage to find a cure.

Very little time is spent actually looking for this antidote, and more is spent doing errands for everyone else around several maps that were considered rather large for the time that the game was released. You'll end up hoofing it and also driving trucks around an island resort, a rampaged city, a dense and humid jungle, and a prison. For some reason, most of the rewards are cash... whatever good that does during the zombie apocalypse. Other times, you'll be given a fancy new weapon modification. There are numerous collectibles to find, and more side-quests than what you'll ever want to actually take on. Fans of Dying Light will be disappointed to learn that there is no parkour here, and much of the running around is actually pretty frustrating considering your character's shoes will feel like they're full of grease any time you try to jump on an object; you'll just slip right off. Even the driving controls are irritating, as they just aren't responsive sometimes when you're trying to turn the steering wheel.

While you're running around Banoi, doing busy work for a host of uninteresting characters with no backstories or stimulating dialogue, you'll be scavenging numerous resources and using various weapons that you find scattered around; from blades to blunts to firearms. These items can be upgraded up to four times each, and modifications can be applied to them as well. However, they do have limited durability, and will break if not repaired when they get worn down. It borrows very heavily from Dead Rising in this regard, but instead of the weapon disappearing altogether, it simply becomes unusable; much like in Dying Light. Most of the gameplay here feels like an exceedingly unpolished version of Dying Light, and Dead Island soon feels a retrospective alpha of the current popular zombie survival title. There's nothing here that hasn't been refined and then done better over the years, and there's honestly very little reason to venture back to it, save for the locations alone. The graphics aren't exactly beautiful thanks to the awful bloom effect, but there are mods that can be used to change that.

Dead Island is a game that you're either going to love or hate. It's a buggy wreck, still some 9 years after its initial release, and its gameplay is solely comprised of fetch quests and escort missions. Hell, the kick mechanic still barely functions, bullets still go right through the enemies (especially if shooting from the hip), and the driving barely works at any given time. The plot is thin, the characters are weak, the weapons are uninteresting, and the dialogue is benign. There's hardly any redeeming qualities here, but what is offered up is some decent, mindless zombie slaughtering mayhem amidst visually pleasing locations such as a tropical island resort and a humid jungle. This Definitive Edition also comes with both the Ryder White and Bloodbath Arena DLCs. It wasn't the top of the charts when it released, and it hasn't aged all that well, but if you're finding yourself quarantined for a couple of weeks then this title might give you the distraction that you need; only if you can get it on a very deep discount.

The best way to describe Dead Island is that it is an honest grind. It is rewarding to play, but more than that, it has gameplay that you can respect. And because its gameplay, simple as it is as a first-person keep-away simulator that consist of the the same gameplay loop from start to end, is so pure and distilled, it comes off as gameplay without conceit, one that compels you to continue squash zombie brains for hours on end.

That doesn't mean this game is not without its problems. Dead Island is overstuffed with repeat content that has you visiting the same locations over and over; exploration is not encouraged, a strange characteristic for an open world game; the story is trite and the added DLC only serves to double down on this distinction; and it shows itself to be insensitive in its portrayal of minority and aboriginal characters. Worse of all, the chapters are arranged from best to worse, leaving the player's expectation with nowhere to go but down after leading off with the resort, easily the best part of the game.

And yet, it does have its charm. Having to deal with the enormous success of its memorable teaser trailer, Dead Island shows itself to be an enduring gem that can easily stand on its own merits. Perhaps the nicest thing to say about Dead Island is that its graphics are too good. (Yes, really. A game about bashing in skulls standing three feet away from you doesn't need draw distances that stretch a mile away.) All the same, the craft and care put into Dead Island makes for an immersive game that gives players exactly what they want: an fulfilling reward-to-time ratio that translates well into a cozy, comforting, chicken noodle-type of game to play.

This is quite the immersive zombie apocalypse game, and for a game from 2016 the graphics are awesome.  Best played in the middle of the night, with headphones on, and by only the glow from a desk lamp's 40-watt bulb.  It's an adreneline rush hearing zombies breathing in the dark shadows surrounding me while I desperately try to figure out where exactly they are before they grab me.

If you only focus on the main campaign tasks and ignore the side quests, you could probably be done in 10 to 15 hours.  But if you do most of the side quests, AND go for all of the achievements, this game should be good for 30 to 40 hours.  Also, there are 4 different characters to choose from, and each of them have various skills and stats, so there is definitely some of replayability here.

There are several different types of zombies to fight here too.  There are slow shufflers, lightning-speed runners, big beefy brawlers who's arms always seem to be longer than yours, suicide bombers, rams ([i]who charge at you like a bull[/i]), floaters ([i]who spit toxic gas at you[/i]), and a few others.  Every time you die, you will lose 10% of your gold, but thankfully none of your inventory items.

Some weapons are found laying around, and some are looted from your kills.  You can find various guns ([i]pistols, rifles, shotguns, etc[/i]), and dozens of different melee weapons.  You can also throw smaller weapons like knives.  At lower levels, you can just punch and kick your way through some fights, but at some point you won't be able to do enough damage with your fists & feet anymore.

All weapons start at level 1.  For a cost, you can upgrade them at workbenches to level 4.  With items you scavenge from all over ([i]wire, tape, metal scrap, timers, alcohol, batteries, hoses, etc[/i]), you can craft customized weapons.  The customized weapons add various extra damages like fire, poison, and shocking.  Of course, there are also scattered merchants where you can buy and sell.

There are trading cards, achievements, and even some Point Shop items.  Some of the achievements are a grind, like finding 120 collectables, and exploring all 72 island locations.  Also, there is co-op available for up to 4 players, and 8 of the achievements require co-op play.  Although I've heard some people complain of a few bugs, I've experienced none myself in the 48 hours I've played so far.

[h1] Review[/h1] 
I played this game back then at release and enjoyed myself a lot and recently got it as part of the franchise pack with Riptide as I never got to play that one. The “definitive” edition is not what it advertises, as the main base game never really had huge content expansions. The only thing of interest is the arena and Ryder class/campaign DLC, which are in itself not that interesting which means its more of a marketing trick.

[u]Gameplay[/u]
Dead Island basically takes the Borderlands gameplay and completely alters it on a zombie focus. You have 4 main classes, each focusing on a specific combat aspect, blunt, sharp, throwing weapons and guns. The latter being rater a niche thing in this game, most weapons you find are useless and those that are useful tend to be used rarely due to the rarity of ammo aside from lategame content.

Weapons have durability and have to be repaired to be used again after a certain amount of time. There are various weapon modifications available, where weapons look completely different and have the chance to add new status effects like electricity. The combat itself is really simple and fun but a bit lackluster as you cannot really block or dodge. Aside from kicking or throwing there isn't much you can do to avoid damage. But the combat that is there is unique enough, atleast for the time it released, to be fine with some shortcomings. There is also a variety of zombie types that slowly get introduced to spice things up.

The classes all have their own rage mode that fills up via kills. This is mostly the biggest difference between those classes, the only other one will be if you either focus on blunt or sharp weapons, the latter being a more common skill shared across the characters. Enemies level with you, so it doesn’t matter if your friend is the first level and you're max level, the main difference is some minor side skills like being able to stomp enemies when downed. This can make certain player levels harder if they focused on non damage upgrades first, or have no damage upgrade available later. Quests itself are also not as interesting, some have unique tasks, but mostly its just grabbing an item and bringing it to someone. Serviceable.
On a side not the game also can be a bit buggy, nothing gamebreaking but noticed glitches here and there.

[u]Story[/u]
The main story of the game is not really interesting side quests even more so,  although the zombie infested island setting is pretty creative. Most of it is there just to give you a goal so you don’t get bored, a reason to continue to the next area and do activities there.

[u]Sound[/u]
Although the main theme is very good, there isnt that much in this game in therms of music. Most of the sound design is very atmospheric, especially the distant zombie screams, wind howling and so on. Combat sounds are also really neat and add a lot to this game.

[u]Graphics[/u]
Especially for its year of release the graphics are amazing. Not only can you cut off enemies limbs, but also break them or make them bleed. Generally the main focus was on the zombies and their movement and reaction to combat. The island itself has also a variety of cool locations and nice effects to them, although it is personally too hard for me on the motion blur and bloom. Animations and models of other side characters can be really awkward and unrealistic though.

[u]Conclusion/TL;DR[/u]
 Now if you look for a coop game with some unique melee combat this one is pretty good. But it has its shortcomings, with some combat design issues and I personally don’t like autolevelling enemies in general which cause non-damage skills to make the game much harder. The island design is really great and a lot of the games systems are really well made for such a unique game. Classes arent that much different aside their rage mode and some passives. In general its a fun game, with a few bugs here and there that dont break the game.

The story of Dead Island is a very cliche tale for a zombie game/movie. You pick from 4 survivors Sam B, Purna, Logan or Xian Mei. They're all stuck on an island of Banoi and after a heavy night of partying they wake up to find the island overrun with the undead and they try to fight their way to safety.

The story itself is abysmal. Most of the story plot points don't make any sense and most of the choices made by the main characters and other survivors are questionable as they put everyone around them in immense danger. The game also really tries hard to make you attached to characters but this doesn't work because of the abysmal voice acting.

Gameplay wise is where Dead Island sort of stands out from other games in the genre. The gameplay mostly consists of melee combat and this is where you learn to fight using everything you find on the ground, like bats, crowbars and planks. You also can craft weaponry which has elemental stats which do even more damage.  There's also a stamina bar which depletes on every attack, once the bar is depleted you are then forced into recovering as you are not able to attack, or run away.

I really enjoyed the original version of Dead Island so when a Linux version of the Definitive Editions was made and went on a deep discount I couldn’t pass it up. Overall I would say that there wasn’t much difference from the normal version. The graphics are a bit better but it’s not like the graphics of the old version were bad. The gameplay is pretty much the same. If you have never tried the old version then I would say to give this a go if you enjoy co-op games or just first person action games in general. I played through solo and had a blast. I never felt like there was a point where the game needed you to have a group of human players to progress. Everything felt doable solo which is something some co-op themed games will fail in. 

	You get to pick from 4 characters to play as. Their backstories don’t really matter because they don’t get much explanation in game. What will matter is what kind of playstyle you prefer. Each character has a different speciality for weapons whether it be blunt weapons, edged weapons, guns, and throwable weapons. You will gain XP for completing quests and killing zombies. You can then use those points to upgrade various skills. It really does a good job of allowing you to tailor the upgrades to how you want to play. There is also a fury mode which when enabled will send you into a frenzy where you can do much more damage then normally which is very useful on hordes or mini boss type enemies. I picked Xian whose speciality was edged weapons. It is very satisfying to hack off zombie legs, arms and heads. When using blunt weapons you can also crush their skulls and bones. 

	There were a few negatives along the way. I pretty much had to turn enhanced navigation on.  With it on it literally gives you a line to follow to your next objective on your map. I don’t like this type of handholding but with it turned off the objective marker on the map would often dissappear for me. I would rather have my hand held then have no idea where to go next. There were also a few points in the game where enemies could shoot me through walls. I could also shoot them but would have no idea they were there until they began shooting because I can’t see though walls. There was also a glitch in the jungle level for a bit. Basically for the first bit in the jungle there were no fast travel options to that area and some side missions would send me back to other areas. I could then not be able to travel back to the jungle once complete. I had to quit the game and reload it and would be auto inserted back in the jungle with my progress intact. This issue went away about halfway through the jungle section. There was also a flickering issue. It would happen maybe once every few hours for about 2-3 seconds and then go away so it wasn’t a major hassle but it is still a bug.

	I played Dead Island Definitive Edition on Linux. It may not show it on Steam but I purchased this game back in 2016. I am just getting around to playing it now due to an issue where the game would crash before loading the main menu. At first I just put the game on the back burner expecting the glitch to be ironed out. I kept reinstalling the game to see if it was fixed but several years later, updates to game, kernel, Mesa drivers, and trying several different distros and the game still had this issue. I finally put time into solving it. What was the cause was a file called “LibGL.so”. The game was made to only work with a specific version of that file. As you can imagine over the years updated versions of that file have been made. The game will crash with anything newer than that version and no distro I tried uses a version that old. The file is also not included with the game, it uses whichever version your OS has installed unless the older one is present. I had to download a copy of the correct version file and drop it into the game folder. Once I did this the game launched just fine. The performance was great as well. I ran the game maxed out at 1080P and my FPS was usually 80-100 or higher. It supported framerates above 60 which was fantastic. There was no manual saving but the game auto saves after every completed task so it isn’t terrible although I would prefer manual save. There was support for Vsync, one AA setting, one ambient occlusion setting, as well as 7 other settings to tweak.  Alt-Tab worked just fine. The game did crash once but just the one time and no more. Not bad for how much time I put into it. My CPU usage during gameplay was usually around 30%, my system RAM usage was usually around 5GB and my VRAM usage was usually around 2.2GB. The game took up 9.22 GB of storage and uses Techland’s own engine called Chrome Engine 5. I played version 1.1.2 of the game.

	I paid $3.30 CAD for Dead Island Definitive Edition. I can say that for how much fun it was it is easily worth $50 CAD. If you enjoy action games, co-op games, zombie games, give it a try if you haven’t already.  It has some bugs and issues but none overshadow the fun I had. I finished a solo playthrough in 26.5 hours.

[H1]Introduction:[/H1] 
I've been meaning to write a review for this game, but the problem is that I have really mixed feelings about it. Parts of it are really fun, hence why I kept playing until the very end, but aspects of it are downright infuriating, thus making this a difficult game to recommend, as I'd hate to steer anyone wrong by suggesting they play it when it's definitely going to get on their nerves, but ultimately, I enjoyed the game enough to finish it, then immediately started playing Dead Island: Riptide, and then I bought Dying Light: Definitive Edition — which is basically a Spiritual Successor to Dead Island — so I suppose I must like it, but then again, maybe I've simply developed Stockholm Syndrome by forcing myself through the at times agonizing experience. Only one way to find out for sure, lets give it a proper review and see how I feel after going through the motions. 

[H1]Visual Presentation:[/H1] 
The graphics in Dead Island: Definitive Edition are a mixed bag. The environments look pretty stunning, especially for a zombie apocalypse style of game which tend to use a rather subdued color palette as well as darker environments as a means to set the mood. In a stark contrast, Dead Island is bright, colorful, and vibrant. There is no night cycle in Dead Island, so the main campaign always takes place in the daytime with the sun blazing overhead, and likewise mostly takes place outdoors, so the game is typically very well-lit, which I honestly appreciate. A lot of horror-themed games go completely overboard these days with darkness, thus making the game difficult to see and practically impossible to play during daylight hours if your TV/Monitor happens to be in a room with windows, so Dead Island is a breath of fresh air in that regard. 
However, the character models leave a lot to be desired as there's very little variety, practically every NPC you meet is represented by variations of a small selection of character models. Furthermore, at times the limitations can lead to some rather comical moments such as encountering NPCs whose appearance really doesn't go with their voice/character. 

[H1]Audio Presentation:[/H1] 
The audio in Dead Island is pretty good, the music goes with the theme while likewise setting the tone. The voice work ranges from good to adequate, with most of the characters performances being convincing enough, perhaps a bit flat at worst. Sound effects are exactly what you'd expect. 

[H1]Gameplay Mechanics:[/H1] 
Despite what the first-person perspective and faux-open-world sandbox style environments may suggest, Dead Island is at it's core, an Action RPG. With a Level Up System, In-depth Skill Trees with an assortment of abilities/perks to unlock, multi-tiered, color-coded, randomly-generated Loot, and every objective in the game is presented in the form of a Quest with Loot, XP, or Money as a reward for completion. While the first-person perspective does lend itself well to shooting, only one of the four playable characters (Purna) is proficient with firearms, you won't find any ammunition until ACT II, and even then firearms just won't be a feasible primary weapon for Purna until you've leveled her up sufficiently and unlocked the appropriate perks in her Skill Tree to loot/craft/carry a sustainable amount of ammunition. For the most part, you'll be relying on melee weapons/abilities in combat. The game features a Crafting System which enables you to craft outlandish augmented weapons, provided that you have obtained the necessary materials/blueprints, which adds much-needed variety to the combat and preventing you from being at the mercy of the game's stingy RNG to obtain effective weapons. 

Unfortunately, this is where the frustration comes in... The melee combat in Dead Island is honestly pretty terrible. Melee attacks feel clunky, you take absurd amounts of damage from ordinary enemy attacks regardless of how much HP you have, and in many areas zombies will infinitely spawn wave after wave, relentlessly advancing upon you until you either complete the objective, exit the area, or die trying. Firearms make the game far easier and more fun to play, but as previously stated, only Purna can make effective use of firearms as a primary weapon, which will take several hours of gameplay. Furthermore, you have to level Purna up specifically for firearms, ignoring any perks which might make her better with melee attacks in the meantime for the eventual payoff of being able to effectively defend yourself from zombies from outside the range of their attacks. Even then, you'll still find yourself raging from time to time when a zombie randomly tosses a plank of wood in your direction and instantly kills you! 
Admittedly, this game was obviously intended to be played cooperatively with three friends online, which would most likely make the game substantially more fun as well as less frustrating to play, but alas, I had no friends who play the game to play with, so I played the game solo. 

[H1]Storytelling:[/H1] 
On the surface, the story in Dead Island is rather straightforward. A viral outbreak has occurred on the resort island of Banoi, transforming the majority of the population into rabid, zombie-like killers who attack and devour uninfected people. Fortunately, these zombies aren't very intelligent at all, so they cannot easily capture people unless they surround them because they're usually pretty slow, can't open doors, can't climb, and make lots of noise, so there are still quite a few survivors who have successfully managed to escape the zombies. Furthermore, all of the playable characters are immune to the virus — or so it seems — and thus can sustain bites/scratches without becoming infected, enabling them to more safely traverse the island in search of survivors, information, and hopefully rescue. More details are revealed as the game progresses, but the story really isn't the primary focus of the game, so it's not very original, nor does it need to be. 

[H1]Performance:[/H1] 
At no point did I ever encounter any serious glitches or issues with performance during the length of my almost 40 hour playthrough. However, it's important to note that this game is several years old at this point, so my PC is way above the recommended specs, and I only played single player. 

[H1]Final Verdict: [/H1] 
For a single player experience, I cannot recommend this game, because although I did enjoy it overall, it's much too frustrating for me to comfortably recommend. However, if you have friends you can play Co-Op with, then it's most likely going to be a much more pleasant, entertaining experience. Again, I must stress that I've never played Co-Op, so I can't say how well it runs with multiple players, but for a game which regularly goes on sale for 75% Off or more, it's definitely worth a shot.

Okay, I expected a lot, but not a game lag every 0,5-2 seconds for 5-8 seconds. From the menu, through "New Game", Character Select, the first cutscene, to the Alt+F4 exit when nothing changed once I got "in-game". Not recommending at all, something needs to be done about the stability of the game first, I'd say.

And yes, the original Dead Island ran fine on my rig. Even DI: Riptide.
